_note: Reported news for the PDF. Compiled every Sunday from the climate-news monitor sources (Eye Radio, Radio Tamazuj, Sudans Post, UN/UNMISS, ReliefWeb, Radio Yei, others); last compiled 2026-10-11. 'counties' lists every county the item names; items with no county go in scope 'national' (state or countrywide). Items older than NEWS_DAYS (21) are dropped.

items.text: No Ebola case in South Sudan; the health system is on high alert after Kenya confirmed a case and with an outbreak in neighbouring DR Congo.

Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation warns of possible Nile flooding along the White Nile system, including around Juba, as Lake Victoria could rise above its historical maximum under El Nino; readings from Nimule to Renk and Nasir to Bentiu are currently falling and below alert levels. It also flags drought effects from the June-September rainfall deficit in Abyei, Pibor and Ruweng.

Heavy rains and insecurity have left Ibba communities more isolated: the roughly 100 km Yambio-Ibba road is almost impassable (deep mud, potholes and flooding), slowing a UNMISS patrol to walking pace.

UNMISS says flooding has submerged about 70% of the land around Bentiu; about 300,000 people shelter behind dykes held by UNMISS and IOM, and a breach not repaired within ten hours could submerge 50,000. IOM faces a shortfall for dyke maintenance and pumping; heavier rain is expected with El Nino from October to February (county inferred from Bentiu).
Lakes State restructured a peace committee citing flood fears; no damage reported (county not stated).

UNMISS-backed peace dialogue in Maban discussed flooding and drought as climate shocks; a paramount chief said the prolonged lack of rain is hurting communities more than ever this year. Early warning and evacuation planning were discussed (no figures given).
40 hepatitis E cases, no deaths, in Northern Bahr el Ghazal (Aweil East, Aweil North, Gok Machar, Aweil West), linked to water contaminated during heavy rains.
Flash flood made the Kapuri bridge overflow and briefly cut movement between Kapuri and Juba (county inferred from location).
Heavy rain flooded shelters in 15 IDP camps across three payams and destroyed homes; residents report no medicines and high food prices.
UNMISS says heavy rain, El Nino and funding shortfalls are straining the temporary dykes kept by IOM and UNMISS at Bentiu (county inferred from Bentiu).
Seven-day oral cholera vaccination drive with MSF and WHO targets 100,000 IDPs after thousands of cases this year.
REACH published a rapid drought impact assessment for Lafon (findings not yet reviewed).
About 1.1 million people affected by a prolonged rainfall deficit across five counties (not named); officials fear more hunger later this year and into 2027.
Uganda warned of record Lake Victoria levels and higher releases into the Nile; Juba and low-lying areas flagged as vulnerable. Nile readings from Nimule to Renk are still below alert levels.
